Welcome to the teaching portal of **Peter Sørensen**.

This site hosts structured course material, lecture notes, slides, and computational demonstrations in quantitative genetics and genomics. All material is reproducible and built using R and Quarto.

---

## 🎓 Courses

### 📘 Quantitative & Population Genetics

Foundations of population and quantitative genetics:

Foundations of population and quantitative genetics:

- Measuring genetic variation (heterozygosity, nucleotide diversity, allele vs. genotype frequencies)  
- Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium and gene pools  
- Mating systems, inbreeding, and their consequences  
- Mutation, migration, recombination, and linkage disequilibrium  
- Genetic drift and natural selection (directional, balancing, purifying)  
- Applications in conservation, medical genetics, and forensics  

Quantitative trait analysis:

- Statistical modeling of complex traits  
- Genetic vs. environmental contributions  
- Broad- and narrow-sense heritability  
- Prediction of offspring phenotypes  
- QTL and association mapping

#### Genetic Variation in Populations
- Measuring genetic variation within populations  
- Heterozygosity, segregating sites, and nucleotide diversity  
- Allele frequencies vs. genotype frequencies  

#### Hardy–Weinberg Equilibrium and Gene Pools
- The gene pool concept  
- Assumptions and biological meaning of Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium  
- Interpreting deviations from equilibrium  

#### Mating Systems and Inbreeding
- Effects of nonrandom mating on genotype frequencies  
- Inbreeding and increased homozygosity  
- Biological consequences of inbreeding  

#### Sources and Structure of Genetic Variation
- Mutation, migration, and recombination  
- Linkage disequilibrium and its decay  

#### Evolutionary Forces
- Genetic drift in finite populations  
- Effects of population size on drift  
- Natural selection and allele frequency change  
- Directional, balancing, and purifying selection  

#### Applications of Population Genetics
- Conservation biology  
- Medical genetics  
- DNA forensics  

#### Quantitative Trait Variation

- Statistical modeling of complex traits  
- Partitioning genetic and environmental contributions  

#### Heritability
- Broad-sense heritability  
- Narrow-sense heritability  
- Predicting offspring phenotypes from parental values  

#### Mapping Quantitative Traits
- Inferring the number of genes affecting a trait  
- QTL mapping  
- Association mapping

## 💻 Teaching Philosophy

The material emphasizes:

- Mathematical foundations  
- Statistical modeling  
- Reproducible research  
- Computational implementation in R  
- Conceptual clarity over memorization  

All lecture material integrates theory, simulation, and applied examples.

---

## 📂 Repository Structure

Each course is structured as a navigable book with:

- Sequential chapters  
- Mathematical notation  
- Executable R code  
- Figures and simulations  
- Narrated slide material where relevant  

---

### Further Reading

Further details on the theory and computation behind Bayesian linear regression, Gibbs sampling, and hierarchical modeling can be found in  
**[Sorensen, D. (2025). *Statistical Learning in Genetics: An Introduction Using R*. Springer.](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-031-86274-8)**  

This book provides a rigorous and accessible introduction to Bayesian modeling, hierarchical inference, and statistical learning methods in **quantitative genetics and genomics**.


### Further Reading

For foundational principles of classical and molecular genetics:

**[Griffiths, A. J. F., Doebley, J. F., Peichel, C. L., & Wassarman, D. A. (2023). *An Introduction to Genetic Analysis* (13th ed.). W. H. Freeman.](https://store.macmillanlearning.com/us/product/Introduction-to-Genetic-Analysis-Digital-Update/p/1319525199)**  


For a unified and modern treatment of quantitative genetics theory and genomics:

**[Walsh, B., Visscher, P. M., & Lynch, M. (2025). *Genetics and Analysis of Quantitative Traits: Foundations* (2nd ed.). Cambridge University Press.](https://global.oup.com/academic/product/genetics-and-analysis-of-quantitative-traits-9780192898180?cc=dk&lang=en&)**  

For Bayesian modeling, hierarchical inference, and statistical learning in quantitative genetics and genomics:

**[Sorensen, D. (2025). *Statistical Learning in Genetics: An Introduction Using R*. Springer.](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-031-86274-8)**  


For likelihood-based and Bayesian inference, including detailed treatment of MCMC methods:

**[Sorensen, D., & Gianola, D. (2002/2010). *Likelihood, Bayesian, and MCMC Methods in Quantitative Genetics*. Springer.](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/b98952)**  


For a comprehensive and mathematically rigorous treatment of modern statistical learning:

**[Hastie, T., Tibshirani, R., & Friedman, J. (2009). *The Elements of Statistical Learning: Data Mining, Inference, and Prediction* (2nd ed.). Springer.](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-0-387-84858-7)**  

For an accessible and application-oriented introduction to statistical learning with R:

**[James, G., Witten, D., Hastie, T., & Tibshirani, R. (2021). *An Introduction to Statistical Learning: With Applications in R* (2nd ed.). Springer.](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-0716-1418-1)**
